problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{2}-6s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{6}{{s}^{2}-6s}=\frac{6}{s(s-6)}=\frac{1}{s-6}-\frac{1}{s}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{6t}} & =\frac{1}{s-6},\,s>6 \\ L{1} & =\frac{1}{s},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}-\frac{1}{s}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}} \\  & ={e}^{6t}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{2}-6s}$ is $f(t)={e}^{6t}-1.$
